subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance use a host-owned default safety bound, remain unbounded unless the new setting is enabled, or wait for a cooperative plugin cancellation contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but the repository's config-surface policy and public plugin semantics do not determine whether compatibility with indefinitely long maintenance outweighs fixing the stall by default.

options.title: Choose a canonical default bound
options.body: Reuse an existing host safety budget or approve one conservative maintenance default, then retain the branch's fencing and fresh-install/upgrade coverage.

options.title: Keep the timeout opt-in
options.body: Merge the new setting disabled by default and explicitly accept that existing deployments remain susceptible until operators configure it.

options.title: Wait for cooperative cancellation
options.body: Pause this approach until the context-engine contract can cancel or safely terminate plugin-owned maintenance rather than only fencing core-owned effects.

recommendation.title: Choose a canonical default bound
recommendation.body: Reuse an existing host safety budget or approve one conservative maintenance default, then retain the branch's fencing and fresh-install/upgrade coverage.
